data.name: Janica
data.gender_notes: Janica is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Slavic name Jana (God is gracious), with the suffix -ica (little, diminutive). The name Janica carries the meaning “God's gracious gift” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Janica usually hope their child will grow to embody god's gracious gift and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the grace and blessings bestowed upon us by God.
data.etymology: Janica belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's gracious gift.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Janica total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_hebrew.meaning: אלוהים הוא חנני - אלוהים רחם עלי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם 'יניקה' נגזר מהמילה העברית 'חנן', שפירושה 'לרחם' או 'להעניק חסד'. הוא קשור קשר הדוק למושג החסד והרחמים האלוהיים, ומשמש כזכר לחסדו ורחמיו של אלוהים על עמו.

in_greek.name: Γιάνη
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα 'Γιάνη' ή 'Ιανικα' συνδέεται με την ελληνική παράδοση και πιθανόν να έχει ρίζες σε სახელizations της Βίβλου ή της Εκκλησίας. Ενδέχεται να συμβολίζει τη σχέση του Θεού με το έλεος και τη χάρη Του.

in_latin.name: Janica
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen 'Janica' in traditione Christiana, potest significare gratiam vel misericordiam Dei. Ea radices habet in cultura Latina et Christiana, et potest referri ad donum vel auxilium divinum.

in_english.name: Janica
in_english.meaning: God is gracious - God has shown favor
in_english.long_meaning: The name 'Janica' is a variant of 'Janet' or 'Jannica', which is believed to derive from the Hebrew name 'Yochanan', meaning 'God is gracious' or 'God has shown favor'. It shares roots with biblical names like 'John', symbolizing divine grace and mercy. Historically, it may relate to early Christian traditions emphasizing God's benevolence.

historical_references.reference: According to legend, Saint Janica was a Roman maiden who was martyred in Dalmatia during the 3rd century. She was said to have converted many to Christianity, and was eventually discovered and executed by her own father for her faith. Her remains were later discovered and venerated in the city of Zadar.

Janica, or Joan of Arc, was a French peasant girl who lived from around 1412 to 1431. She claimed to have divine visions from God, and led the French army to several victories during the Hundred Years' War against England. She was later captured and put on trial for heresy and witchcraft, and was burned at the stake at the age of 19.
